A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICW research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, robustness and text-quality experiments for four ICW strategies, using ELI5 questions and ICLR papers, alongside ablations and attack evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds conversation-length, output-length, GPTZero-comparison and prompt-override results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The four watermark-generation strategies, detector statistics, two-stage Lexical IPI adaptation and exploratory appendix variants are retained. The new material analyzes and evaluates these procedures without establishing a changed watermarking algorithm.

E1.justification: ELI5 and the 2020–2023 ICLR-paper dataset remain unchanged. v2 extends scenario coverage to sustained multi-turn conversations and IPI inputs containing an adversarial counterinstruction; it adds no new dataset, language or application domain.

E2.justification: GPTZero, previously cited but not experimentally compared, becomes an evaluated DTS comparator in v2 Table 9. PostMark and YCZ+23 retain their participation in the corresponding original comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify ten-turn conversations, 1,000-word outputs, an IPI counterinstruction before the review prompt, and TPR at 4% FPR for the GPTZero comparison. These supplement the original protocols; the previously reported models, sample counts, metrics and 300-word evaluations are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds analyses of instruction persistence over ten turns, sensitivity to longer outputs, and resistance to an 'ignore prior prompts' attack. These substantially broaden the robustness questions tested. The earlier vocabulary-length ablation, token-wise experiment and adaptive paraphrasing attack remain present.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The perplexity distributions and Acrostics resampling estimator are retained. The new theoretical false-alarm bound does not add uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: The original numerical results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial evidence in Tables 7–9 and 11. Length evaluations report ROC-AUCs of 0.995–1.000 and 0.998–1.000; GPTZero obtains 0.890 TPR at 4% FPR versus 0.964–1.000 for ICWs; the new IPI attack yields ROC-AUCs of 0.993–0.996. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over matched v1 results.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix B and Theorem B.1, absent from v1. It adapts a cited concentration bound to Lexical ICW, defines word-frequency statistics and an input-dependent false-alarm threshold, and states an Initials extension. This introduces substantive formal analysis, although the Initials extension is not derived.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: prompt-only watermarking through four strategies, applicability to DTS and IPI, and dependence on model capabilities. Added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains why miss-detection analysis lacks a suitable instruction-following model and why Acrostics false-alarm analysis remains unresolved. v2 also corrects the Lexical robustness explanation to match its verb/adverb/adjective vocabulary. The existing adaptive-attack limitations are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and discloses the full IPI paper-review prompt in Appendix A.2. The latter documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed review procedure. Existing implementation settings and vocabulary-processing details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds ten cited works, including research on image/audio watermarking, watermark ensembles, dataset-use detection and stakeholder incentives. The basic post-hoc/in-process positioning remains. Appendix B also gives the previously cited Zhao et al. work a direct theoretical role.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative are retained. Related work becomes a standalone section, the main-text adaptive-attack discussion moves into the appendix, and ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added. Local wording, terminology, affiliations and citation style are revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact results tables and redraws Figure 3 with attack titles and simpler legends while retaining its curves and values. Existing tables and examples are resized and relocated within the ICLR layout; the remaining figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The GPTZero comparison and new persistence, output-length and prompt-override tests strengthen practical validation, while the review prompt and code link improve reproducibility information. The gains are incremental: headline results remain unchanged, new experiments lack uncertainty reporting, and Appendix B states rather than derives its Initials extension despite the reproducibility statement's promise of complete proofs.
